coaching.headline: A soft start, then we won every fight that counted and walked Orb Prime straight into their Core.
coaching.team: We started sloppy. Two of our outer towers fell before we took one, and they got the first Fangtooth and the Mini Prime while all five of us were alive. After that we stopped giving shit away: we never lost a fight, turned all five we won into objectives or structures, and took nine structures to their three. Skylar, Willy Guggenheim and Bayle did the killing.

focus.title: Show up for the early majors
focus.action: Before the first Fangtooth and the Mini Prime spawn, decide out loud: all five contest, or we take a tower somewhere else at the same time. Watching them take it with nobody dead does not happen again.

40.7.call: Scarlett opened on Grux, Skylar dropped Legion and Gideon, Steel finished Kwang, and the team lost nobody. Orb Prime followed, then the base fell. That is how a game gets closed: win the fight, take the prize, then walk straight to the Core.

32.4.call: Skylar died first, to Legion, and the team still turned the fight 4-1 while the enemy outer and inner towers fell. One allied outer tower dropped in the same window, so the trade still came out ahead on structures.

29.9.call: Willy Guggenheim's double kill on Legion and Adele started it, Bayle finished Grux, and their outer tower fell in the same window. Skylar was the only loss, to Gideon. Kill the backline, take the tower, reset: repeat that every time.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Goldilocks324 ran a proper fucking support game: zero deaths, the most wards placed and cleared on our team, a hand in more than half our kills, and more damage mitigated than any of us.

Gideon did the most damage on their side and landed more kills than any of them. Steel's stuns go on Gideon before Black Hole: Truesilver Bracelet makes Gideon immune to crowd control while its shield holds after the ultimate.
a2319134-808e-4456-853f-cf3a14be22fc: Skylar ran the hardest carry game in the lobby: our highest hero damage, the most kills in the game, and Adele dead four times. Killing their only healer that often is exactly the right priority. Keep that shit.
Grux and Kwang both carry stuns. Hold Liberator's cleanse for one of those so Skylar keeps shooting instead of eating the follow-up.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Cuban Noobster ate the second most damage on the team and died once, early, to Grux. Soaking that much damage for a single death is what a frontline offlane is supposed to look like.

Scarlett's late kills on Legion and Grux came in the fights around Primal Fangtooth and Orb Prime. Same standard next game: when a late major is up, Swan Song goes on their nearest damage dealer and the team follows.
e6883bce-af43-4199-9d79-d7125804b8e3: First blood, three kills on Kwang, the most objective damage on the team and only two deaths. Bayle soaked more damage than anyone in the game and kept swinging like a drunk at closing time.
The early Fangtooth and the Mini Prime still went to them for free. Bayle runs the early objective clock: start the clear toward the pit before each spawn so the team has a jungler to group on.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy Guggenheim farmed like a bastard, finished with the most gold in the game, and actually spent it on people: seven kills for two deaths.
Both deaths went to Gideon. Before trading, park Void Drone on Gideon to drain that big mana pool, then Neural Disruptor hits harder for the mana Gideon is missing.

matchup: Adele roots and mesmerizes and was their only listed healer; Legion slows and knocks back.
Gideon was their top damage with magical burst; Grux and Kwang were the lockdown threats.
build: Dynamo makes immobilized enemies take more damage, paying off with Steel's stuns.
Gaia Greaves and Flux Matrix cover both armors, and Legion, Grux, Adele and Gideon gave both a target.
eternal: Krix and Cannibalism add health, and Cannibalism suits a player with this many assists.
Festering Wounds is a draft alternative to Voracity, trading small kill sustain for anti-heal, though the team had four anti-heal items.
augment: Heavy Metal scales with total armor, so every armor item feeds it and the build pulls the same way.
Colossal Crash is the alternative for a longer, wider Shield Slam, trading the knockup for a knockback.
crest: Leafsong's Phantom Rush gives allies speed and slow immunity, with clear uses against this lobby's many slows.
The extra ward capacity sits alongside the highest ward count on our team.
improvement: With zero deaths and four anti-heal items on the team, the current build is a sound keep.
Tainted Charm is the swap if enemy healing starts winning fights, cutting Adele's and Grux's healing just by standing near.
It gives up Tainted Guard's armor and some Heavy Metal damage.

matchup: The only early duo deaths were Adele's, both to Skylar.
Adele's Queen's Garden pulls flying enemies down, a direct answer to Air Assault.
Later threats were Gideon's burst and tether root, plus stuns from Grux and Kwang.
build: Hypercharge carries Sky Splitter, Tainted Rounds and Viper's effects on Skylar's shots.
Tainted Rounds cut Adele's and Grux's healing; Viper helps against Kwang's Stonewall and Adele's armor.
eternal: Thraex, Savage Strikes and Rallying Roar mark, heal and speed up the team after Atomiser.
Ferocity is the alternative to Rallying Roar for long fights, trading the team speed burst for ramping attack speed.
augment: Assault MK-II rewards fights where Skylar stays airborne and shooting.
Adele's ultimate pulling flying enemies down is the main counter.
Plasma Barrage is the alternative if grenade damage on low-health targets matters more than hover time.
crest: Liberator cleanses all debuffs with a short shield, with clear targets in Grux's and Kwang's stuns, Adele's roots and Gideon's root.
The match cannot show which of those it answered.
improvement: Against Kwang's and Grux's health and armor, Sky Splitter is a sound keep.
Imperator over Sky Splitter is the swap for squishy targets, trading current-health damage, lifesteal and attack speed for bigger crits.

matchup: Kwang tethers, knocks up, stuns and slows, and built magical with Tainted Scepter's anti-heal.
Legion and Grux brought the physical damage and Gideon the magical burst.
build: Tainted Blade, Mutilator, Terminus and Solaris make a sustain build that must keep hitting heroes to stay alive.
Mistmeadow Buckler answers magical damage and Rebirth resurrects after a short delay.
eternal: Marrow, Blood Bank and Roses stack healing with the lifesteal items.
Kwang's Tainted Scepter and Legion's Tainted Trident cut that healing when they land.
Jealousy is a draft alternative to Roses, trading takedown gold for more low-health damage.
augment: Volcaic Slam leaves a damaging, slowing rupture, but only when Ashen Vow's outer edge hits heroes.
Scarlet Dawn is the alternative for more frequent First Intent dashes and shields, trading the slow zone for mobility.
crest: Liberator cleanses all debuffs, with a clear purpose against Kwang's knockup and Grux's pull and stuns.
Swan Song's Unstoppable backflip covers part of the same need during the ultimate.
improvement: Nothing beyond Mistmeadow Buckler adds armor, and no physical armor against Legion and Grux.
Scarlett died once, so this game never punished it.
If physical damage wins the frontline trade, swap physical armor into Terminus's slot, trading lifesteal shielding for protection.

matchup: Grux pulls, drags and stuns, and heals on every hero hit.
Bayle's main target was Kwang, killed three times including first blood.
build: Tainted Trident directly answers Grux's and Adele's healing.
The Perforator cuts through Kwang's Stonewall, and Citadel adds armor per nearby enemy hero.
Rebirth resurrects after a short delay.
eternal: Thraex, Savage Strikes and Ferocity, with Swift Strikes and Berserk, all reward staying on one target.
Golden Mane is the defensive alternative to Ferocity if burst ends the brawl early.
augment: Swift Strikes suits weaving abilities between attacks with a post-cast attack speed burst.
Frenzied Fighter is the alternative, keeping Berserk active at low health, trading that rhythm for a stronger low-health brawl.
crest: Judgement's Thunder Cleaver deals area damage and heals on hero hits, matching Bayle's brawling.
The crest's share of the team-high healing is not recorded.
improvement: Bayle's off-core anti-heal, armor-penetration and survival build fits this lobby and is a sound keep.
If Grux's pull and stuns end fights before Berserk matters, compare tenacity in Rebirth's slot, trading the second life.

matchup: Gideon was the mid opponent and top enemy damage, with a slowing comet, delayed tether root and Black Hole pull.
Truesilver Bracelet gives him a shield and crowd-control immunity after his ultimate.
build: Combustion, Noxia, Oblivion Crown and Wraith Leggings stack magical burst.
Caustica ignores part of magical armor, useful against Grux's Absolution and Adele's Xenia.
Void Conduit gives magical armor against Gideon, plus omnivamp and mana regeneration while near an ally.
eternal: Aion and Philosopher fuel economy, sitting alongside the most gold in the game.
Void Conduit's mana regeneration supports Runic Focus.
Perfection is the alternative to Runic Focus, giving ability haste at high health instead of mana-scaled power.
augment: Combat Veteran is an economy pick adding speed and passive experience, matching the Aion setup.
Devastating Bombs suits isolated targets and Pulsefire Rounds adds basic attack damage; both give up the experience.
crest: Soulbearer's Anima gives a shield, magical lifesteal and movement speed: the defensive button against Gideon's burst.
improvement: Keep Caustica unless Gideon keeps finding kills.
Then another magical armor item over Caustica trades penetration against Grux and Adele for survival.
Void Conduit already answers Gideon's magic.

threats: Chain-CC risk (2 hard-CC abilities, ~1.0s of lockdown): Kwang Surge of the Heavens (knockup 0.5s), Grux Crush (knockup 0.5s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Heal-stacking: Adele. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought 4 items of it.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Bayle Kingslayer (knockback), Lt. Belica Neural Disruptor (silence 0.5s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

loadout.name: Volcaic Slam
loadout.text: Empowered Cindara leaves behind a rupture that erupts after 0.5s. The eruption deals 20 (+4 per Level) (+25%) Damage to Enemies and Slows by 40% for 1.25s.
loadout.plain: When an outer-edge Ashen Vow hit empowers your next Cindara, that lantern slam also leaves a rupture that erupts and slows. It gives your Ashen Vow into Cindara combo a second hit and makes it hard to walk out of.

loadout.name: Marrow
loadout.text: Heal for 6%/7%/8%/9% of damage dealt to Heroes, increased up to 15%/20%/25%/30% based on your Missing Health. (65% effectiveness for AoE attacks, 15% against monsters.)
loadout.plain: Heals you for part of your damage to heroes, more the lower your health. Minueta's stabs and Swan Song's strike are big hits, so this keeps a diving Scarlett alive when the fight drags on.

loadout.name: Blood Bank
loadout.text: Store 100% of Hero damage as charges for 3s. Gain 0.75% Lifesteal per 100 charges.
loadout.plain: Your recent hero damage turns into extra lifesteal. Minueta's stabs already benefit from lifesteal, so a big combo into a hero makes the rest of your stabs and swings heal more.

loadout.name: Roses
loadout.text: Takedowns grant 20 bonus gold per previous takedown, capped at +100g (5 takedowns). Hero kills also grant +50% effectiveness of Marrow’s Major for 8s.
loadout.plain: Takedowns pay extra gold that grows with each takedown, and hero kills briefly boost Marrow's healing. A snowball piece for a Scarlett who is already winning fights with Swan Song.

loadout.name: Liberator
loadout.text: Purifying Guard:  Cleanse all Debuffs. Gain a 80 (+100%) Shield for 2.5s.
loadout.plain: Removes every debuff and gives you a shield. Save it for the slow or stun that would stop your First Intent dash, then go back in.

loadout.name: Swift Strikes
loadout.text: After casting an ability, Bayle gains 45% Attack Speed for one attack. Additionally, he automatically starts with the 3rd attack in his Basic Attack chain, but it always deals 20% decreased damage.
loadout.plain: Every ability cast speeds up Bayle's next swing, and his attack chain opens on the heavy third hit, at reduced damage. Weave a basic attack after each ability for quick bursts.

loadout.name: Thraex
loadout.text: Mark the last Enemy Hero damaged by your Basic Attack for 3s, increasing your damage against them by 3% (+0.4% per level) and reducing the damage they deal to you by 1.5% (+0.35% per level).

loadout.text: Deal 1.5 (+0.4 per level) Physical Damage On-Hit. Attacking an Enemy Hero increases this by 100% for 3s, stacking up to 3 times. Heal for the damage dealt.

loadout.name: Ferocity
loadout.text: Gain 1% Total Attack Speed per 1s in Hero Combat, stacking infinitely.
loadout.plain: Attack speed keeps rising each second Bayle stays in a hero fight, so long fights favor Bayle more as they go. Weak in quick skirmishes.

loadout.name: Judgement
loadout.text: Thunder Cleaver:  Deal 70 (+40%) Damage in an area around you. On Hero hit, Heal (+30%) (+8%). Subsequent Hero hits Heal for 50% effectiveness.
loadout.plain: Activate mid-fight to hit everyone around him and heal on each hero hit; the first heals fully, the rest at 50%. Use after Skull Crusher lands him in the crowd.
